items.title: Custer Speaker Series events announced for fall 2026
items.summary: In November, the next talk will be by Jason Tedrow, B.S.E.'97, president and CEO of InProduction. On Wednesday, Nov. 4, at 1 p.m. in the Parkview Room (D-132), Tedrow will present, “From the Shop Floor to the C-suite: An Engineer's Path to the Corner Office.”
items.source: WMU College of Engineering and Applied Sciences

items.title: From Engineer to Entrepreneur: How Talal Arshad turned global ambitions into a thriving local business
items.summary: Arshad first came to Kalamazoo from Pakistan to pursue a degree in aerospace engineering at Western Michigan University.
items.source: WMU International Student and Scholar Services

items.title: Multihyphenate alumna Kelly Burris is a highflyer
items.summary: The Western alumna, BS ’88, and recently elected vice chair of the University’s Board of Trustees, has been an aerospace engineer, a licensed pilot and an intellectual property attorney.

items.title: Western set to compete with top U.S. universities in the EcoCAR Innovation Challenge
items.summary: KALAMAZOO, Mich.—Western Michigan University is taking the wheel as one of only 20 universities nationwide selected for the highly competitive EcoCAR Innovation Challenge.
items.source: WMU College of Engineering and Applied Sciences

items.title: Lemmer named John O. Hallquist Endowed Professor in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
items.summary: KALAMAZOO, Mich.— Dr. Kristina M. Lemmer, a leading researcher in plasma and electric propulsion for spacecraft, has been named a John O. Hallquist Endowed Professor in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering at Western Michigan University.
items.source: WMU College of Engineering and Applied Sciences

items.title: All systems go: Aerospace engineering student launches work into space
items.summary: The aerospace engineering master’s student followed the glowing arch of the SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket on March 30 as it carried Transporter-16—with his payload, the Western Aerospace Thin-Sat, on board—into the ionosphere.
